ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure has two schematic diagrams, A and B, of day-night distribution in the Southern Hemisphere at the same time, with shading indicating night. In the two diagrams, the shaded night area in the lower part of the Southern Hemisphere and on the high-latitude side is relatively obvious, indicating that the high-latitude areas of the Southern Hemisphere have long nights and are in winter, so the direct solar point should be in the Northern Hemisphere. Reasoning: The angle between the plane of the twilight circle and the equatorial plane and the absolute value of the latitude of the direct solar point are complementary, so when the angle is 70°, the absolute value of the latitude of the direct solar point is 20°. Combined with the Southern Hemisphere being in winter in the figure, it can be determined that the Sun directly shines at 20°N. Sanya, Hainan is located at about 18°N, lower than the latitude of the direct solar point, that is, south of the direct solar point. The beach umbrella shadow is shortest at local noon; at noon the Sun is located due north of Sanya, and the shadow is opposite to the direction of the Sun, so the shadow faces south.
